stories.title: RBI weighs rate hike as India‑G7 interest‑rate gap and inflation risks rise
stories.summary: The Reserve Bank of India said its monetary‑policy outlook is being shaped by the interest‑rate gap with G7 economies and by rising inflation and input‑cost pressures. Recent GDP data show resilience, driven by strong private consumption and exports. YES Bank projects that the RBI could implement a cumulative 50‑basis‑point rate increase.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Two killed, eight injured in attack at Dammam’s King Fahd International Airport
stories.summary: Two people – a Saudi citizen and an Indian resident – were killed and eight others were injured in an incident at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, eastern Saudi Arabia, on Wednesday evening. The General Authority of Civil Aviation said it had not identified the type of attack. Earlier that day a drone intercepted over the Eastern Province caused two deaths near an Aramco processing facility.
stories.why: The event highlights ongoing security risks to Saudi civilian and energy sites.

stories.title: RBI raises repo rate by 25 basis points as inflation risks widen
stories.summary: The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee increased the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to curb rising inflation. Governor Sanjay Malhotra said inflation is becoming more generalized, with many commodities above 4%, and Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta cited external supply‑side shocks affecting inflation outlook. External members warned that an aggressive hike could slow economic growth.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.

stories.title: Vance tells Republicans to 'stop whining' about controversial Ohio attack ad
stories.summary: JD Vance urged fellow Republicans to stop "whining" about an Ohio campaign ad showing Democratic candidate Amy Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, calling her a liar. The ad, credited to Vivek Ramaswamy's campaign, has been paid for with millions of dollars for statewide placement. Acton's brother condemned it as turning alleged sexual assault into a political talking point.
stories.why: The GOP split over the ad shows disagreement on whether to defend or criticize it, and millions spent on statewide placement make it a strategic issue for the party.
stories.previousTitle: JD Vance urges Republicans to stop criticizing Ohio attack ad
stories.previousSummary: JD Vance told fellow Republicans to stop “whining” about a controversial Ohio campaign advertisement that featured Donna Arthur, the estranged mother of Democratic candidate Amy Acton, accusing her daughter of lying her entire life. The ad did not mention that Arthur’s husband had been charged with raping Acton as a child. The campaign of Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy claimed credit for the ad and spent millions on statewide broadcasts, while Acton’s brother condemned it as a “despicable low.”
